Verdict

No confirmed malicious supply-chain compromise indicators — overall risk: info.

Malicious Supply-Chain Indicators

No confirmed malicious supply-chain indicators.

Automatic Execution Paths

  • pyproject.toml uses the standard setuptools.build_meta build backend.
  • No setup.py, .pth, sitecustomize.py, usercustomize.py, or custom install-time build hook evidence was identified in the provided corpus.
  • No entry_points or install/interpreter-start automatic execution evidence was identified.
  • scripts/install_micromamba.sh and scripts/setup_environment.sh appear to be user-invoked helper scripts, with no evidence that they run automatically during package installation.

Theft / Exfiltration / Persistence / Lateral Movement / Stealth

  • Credential harvesting: no code was identified that broadly searches environment variables, .env files, SSH keys, cloud/CI tokens, wallet files, or registry tokens.
  • Exfiltration: no upload to attacker-controlled C2, webhooks, raw IPs, or paste/drop services was identified.
  • Staging: no evidence of collecting files into tar/zip/gzip/base64 archives for transfer was identified.
  • Persistence: no cron, systemd, launch agent, shell profile modification, background loop, or self-reinstall logic was identified.
  • Lateral movement: no evidence of Kubernetes, Docker socket, cloud metadata, or GitHub Actions/CI token abuse was identified.
  • Obfuscation/loader behavior: torch.compile() and eval() appear to be normal PyTorch model optimization/evaluation usage, not malicious loader evidence.

Distribution Integrity Anomalies

  • The .pypirc reference in .gitignore appears to be a normal Python .gitignore sensitive-file exclusion entry, not credential theft evidence.
  • Included figures/*.png, docs/index.html, and scripts/*.sh files are explainable as documentation, experiment results, and environment setup helpers; no hidden payload or native binary evidence was identified.
  • scripts/install_micromamba.sh contains curl -Ls https://micro.mamba.pm/install.sh | bash, but it is a user-invoked environment setup script and there is no evidence it runs automatically during package installation.
  • Sudden dependency insertion, typosquatting, wheel/sdist mismatch, or unexpected executable payloads were not confirmed from the provided material.

Additional Verification Needed

  • The input is centered on selected extracted text, so a complete manual review of all 78 files is limited.
  • PNG and other binary/large files were not content-decoded to conclusively rule out embedded payloads.
  • A comparison between the PyPI sdist and the GitHub source repository, as well as prior-version dependency diffs, would be needed for stronger integrity assurance.
  • Supply-chain risk in dependencies such as baloot and hl_gauss_pytorch was not assessed from this package artifact alone.
